Condensed Points of Focus by Criteria Group (Points of focus are illustrative characteristics used to judge design/operating effectiveness — not independently required. Condensed to essential themes per group; consult full source for the complete COSO-aligned enumeration if needed for engagement-level testing detail.) CC1 (Control Environment): tone at the top; documented standards of conduct; competence-based hiring/training; accountability structures/incentives; board independence and cybersecurity expertise; consideration of contractors/vendor personnel in conduct standards. CC2 (Info & Communication): identifies information requirements; classifies/manages information assets and their physical/virtual location; documents data flows; internal communication of responsibilities, incidents, and objective changes; security/privacy awareness training; external communication channels (incl. whistleblower lines) and incident-reporting methods to external users. CC3 (Risk Assessment): clear objective-setting (operations, compliance, reporting); identifies threats (intentional/unintentional/environmental) and vulnerabilities across system components; analyzes threats/vulnerabilities from vendors/business partners; assesses fraud risk (incl. IT-related fraud); assesses changes in environment, business model, leadership, technology, and vendor relationships. CC4 (Monitoring): blend of ongoing and separate evaluations (audits, vulnerability scans, pen tests, third-party assessments); baseline understanding; timely communication and tracking of deficiency remediation. CC5 (Control Activities): control activities tied to risk assessment; mix of manual/automated and preventive/detective controls; segregation of duties; technology general controls (infrastructure, security management, acquisition/development/maintenance); policies deployed via documented procedures with assigned accountability. CC6 (Logical & Physical Access): asset inventory/classification; access restriction via authentication (incl. MFA where risk-appropriate) and network segmentation/zero trust; credential lifecycle management (creation, periodic review, timely revocation); least privilege and segregation of duties via role-based access; encryption of data at rest/in transit and cryptographic key protection; physical access creation/removal/review and device recovery; secure decommissioning/data destruction; boundary protection (firewalls, IDS/IPS, endpoint detection); data loss prevention for transmission/removable media/endpoints; anti-malware and change-control for software; scanning inbound assets for malware. CC7 (System Operations): configuration hardening standards and monitoring; file-integrity/change- detection tooling; periodic vulnerability scanning with timely remediation; anomaly detection across physical, credential-based, and external-access vectors; defined incident detection/response/containment/remediation/restoration procedures with assigned roles; post-incident root-cause analysis and control improvements; periodic recovery-plan and incident-response testing. CC8 (Change Management): change authorization, secure design/development, documentation, testing (unit/integration/regression/security), approval, and controlled deployment across the full system life cycle; segregation of duties in deployment; emergency-change and patch-management processes; baseline configuration management; (Availability) considers system resilience in design; (Confidentiality/Privacy) protects confidential/personal information through the change process and applies privacy-by-design. CC9 (Risk Mitigation): business-disruption risk mitigation planning (incl. insurance where appropriate); vendor/business-partner risk lifecycle — requirements-setting, vulnerability identification, periodic risk assessment/tiering, accountability assignment, communication/exception protocols, performance assessment, and termination procedures (incl. safe data return/removal); confidentiality/privacy commitments obtained from and compliance assessed for vendors. A (Availability): capacity measurement/forecasting tied to change management; environmental-threat identification and protection mechanisms (power, fire, water, etc.); data backup procedures, offsite storage, alternate/redundant processing infrastructure, ransomware-aware recoverability planning; periodic business-continuity and backup-integrity testing. C (Confidentiality): defining/identifying confidential information at creation/receipt; retention limited to purpose (unless law requires otherwise); protection from destruction during retention; identification and secure destruction procedures at end of retention. PI (Processing Integrity): defined functional/nonfunctional requirements and data definitions (population, elements, sources, units, accuracy, time period); input completeness/accuracy validation and recordkeeping; defined processing specifications/activities with error detection/correction and activity logging; output protection, correct distribution, and completeness/accuracy controls; storage protection/archiving and complete/accurate storage recordkeeping. P (Privacy): comprehensive, current, accessible privacy notice covering purpose, choice/consent, collection, use/retention/disposal, access, disclosure, security, quality, monitoring; implicit/explicit consent management (explicit required for sensitive data and new uses); collection minimization via fair/lawful means from reliable sources; use limited to stated purposes; retention/disposal limited to necessity with secure destruction; data-subject access/correction rights with denial notification; disclosure only to consented, contractually-bound third parties with authorized/unauthorized-disclosure recordkeeping; vendor privacy commitments and breach-notification obligations; breach/incident notification to data subjects/regulators; PI quality (accuracy/completeness/relevance) maintenance; complaint-handling and ongoing compliance monitoring with corrective/disciplinary action. 7. Key Definitions (Glossary Highlights) Term Definition Access to personal information Ability to view (and often update/correct) PI held by an organization Authentication Verifying identity/attributes claimed by an entity, or verifying source/integrity of data Data controller Organization that (alone or jointly) determines the purposes and means of processing personal data Data processor Organization that processes personal data at the direction of a data controller Data subject The individual about whom personal information is collected Commitments Management's declarations to customers re: system performance (contracts, SLAs, published statements) System requirements Specifications for how a system should function to meet commitments, laws/regulations, and other objectives Security event Occurrence from actual/attempted unauthorized access/use that impairs or could impair CIA of information/systems Security incident A security event requiring action to protect information assets/resources Residual risk Risk remaining after management's response has been designed and implemented Vulnerability Weakness in a system component (incl. information assets, procedures, controls) that could be exploited/triggered Explicit consent Individual actively signifies agreement through affirmative communication Implied consent Consent reasonably inferred from action/inaction (e.g., not opting out) SOC 2 examination Reports on whether the system description is per criteria, controls are suitably designed (Type 1), and — for Type 2 — operated effectively over a period, based on applicable TSC 8. Application Note for Compliance-Gap Tooling Unlike GDPR (flat article numbering) or HIPAA (Standard → R/A implementation specification), SOC 2's structure is Common Criteria (mandatory baseline for every engagement) + category- specific
